question: In which part of the Constitution of India is the procedure for amendments in the Constitution laid down?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XX**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The procedure for amendments in the Constitution of India is laid down in **Part XX** of the Constitution.
 
• **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
 
• An amendment can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either House of Parliament.
 
• The Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Amendments:**

 
 
• Some amendments require a simple majority in Parliament.
 
• Others require a special majority, i.e., a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting.
 
• Amendments affecting federal provisions require the ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Significant Amendments:**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, known as the "Mini-Constitution," brought about widespread changes.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act, 1978, reversed many provisions of the 42nd Amendment.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• The power of judicial review allows the Supreme Court and High Courts to determine the constitutional validity of amendments.
 
• The landmark case of Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) established the Basic Structure Doctrine, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Amendment Process:**
 
 
• The process ensures that amendments are not made lightly and that there is a broad consensus.
 
• This process is designed to be a balance between rigidity and flexibility, ensuring stability while allowing necessary changes.
